name: Central bank stress
summary: Bank of England raised rates to 4% on 5 Nov; euro inflation at 4% adds pressure for an ECB hike
state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, as the energy shock lifts inflation (Sovereign Magazine). Euro-area inflation reached 4.0% in October and the ECB is expected to raise rates into a stalling economy (European Business Magazine). Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency or inter-meeting move had been made as of 7 Nov.
for_you: Higher policy rates tend to feed through to mortgage and loan costs over the following months.
rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma at major central banks = Watch; no emergency moves (Alert)

sources.title: Sovereign Magazine — Bank of England rate rise, November 2026
European Business Magazine — Eurozone inflation hits 4% as ECB prepares to raise rates

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
